pp.source: Perforant path volley, rabbit in vivo (Lomo 1971).

mf.source: Mossy fibre, mouse slices (Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger 2008).

ca1.source: Pyramidal axon, assumed like CA3 (Meeks & Mennerick 2007).

mc.source: Mossy-cell axon, assumed like mossy fibres (slower in imaging: Ma et al. 2017).

synapse.source: Monosynaptic delay after the perforant-path volley (Lomo 1971).

dend.source: EPSP spread to the soma, a few ms (assumed).

fire.source: Spike start at the axon initial segment, 20-30 um out (Schmidt-Hieber et al. 2008).

pp_spine.title: Perforant-path bouton on a granule-cell spine
pp_spine.say: A small glutamatergic bouton on a dendritic spine, far out on the dendrite. AMPA and NMDA receptors; each synapse is weak, so many must arrive together.

mf_giant.title: Giant mossy-fibre bouton on a thorny excrescence
mf_giant.say: One of the largest synapses in the brain: a bouton 4-10 um across wrapped around a cluster of spines (a thorny excrescence) on the CA3 cell's proximal dendrite, with dozens of release sites. Weak at rest, it facilitates hugely with repeated firing: a conditional detonator.

mf_thorn_mc.title: Mossy-fibre bouton on a mossy-cell thorn
mf_thorn_mc.say: In the hilus the granule-cell axon gives large boutons onto the thorny excrescences of mossy cells, the hilar counterpart of the CA3 contact.

mc_iml.title: Mossy-cell bouton in the inner molecular layer
mc_iml.say: Mossy-cell axons end on the proximal dendrites of granule cells in the inner third of the molecular layer, mostly at other levels and on the other side.

sc_spine.title: Schaffer-collateral bouton on a CA1 spine
sc_spine.say: Small en-passant boutons on CA1 spines in stratum radiatum and oriens: the most studied synapse in neuroscience (LTP).

rc_spine.title: Recurrent-collateral bouton on a CA3 spine
rc_spine.say: CA3 cells excite each other in radiatum and oriens: the autoassociative network that can complete a pattern from a fragment.

ta_spine.title: Temporoammonic bouton on a CA1 tuft spine
ta_spine.say: EC layer III axons end on the distal tuft of CA1 cells in stratum lacunosum-moleculare.

inh_dend.title: GABAergic bouton on a distal dendrite
inh_dend.say: Dendrite-targeting inhibition: GABA-A synapses on the dendritic shaft right where the excitatory input of that layer arrives.

inh_peri.title: Basket-cell terminals around a soma
inh_peri.say: Perisomatic inhibition: many fast GABA-A boutons from one basket cell on the cell body, timing when the cell can fire.

inh_ais.title: Chandelier cartridge on the axon initial segment
inh_ais.say: Axo-axonic terminals line up along the axon initial segment, where the spike starts.

rides.label: Trisynaptic loop
rides.blurb: Entorhinal cortex to dentate to CA3 to CA1 to subiculum, riding four whole-brain tracings that touch in the atlas.

steps.title: An entorhinal layer II cell fires
steps.say: MouseLight AA1047, a layer II cell of the lateral entorhinal cortex, traced through the whole brain (Winnubst 2019). Its axon is the lateral perforant path.
steps.lab: Layer II of the entorhinal cortex is where dentate spikes start: a lateral volley gives DS1, a medial one DS2.

steps.title: Down the perforant path
steps.say: The axon leaves layer II, runs through the angular bundle, perforates the subiculum and crosses the hippocampal fissure into the dentate molecular layer.

velocity.source: Perforant path volley, rabbit in vivo (Lomo 1971).

steps.title: Synapse on a granule-cell dendrite
steps.say: The axon passes 6.6 um from granule cell AA0573's dendrite in MML2 (shifted 6.6 um to touch): a perforant-path spine synapse.
steps.lab: This molecular-layer synapse is the current sink you see at DS1 (outer third) and DS2 (middle third).

steps.title: Inward to the soma
steps.say: The EPSP spreads from the distal dendrite to the cell body.

steps.title: The granule cell fires
steps.say: Granule cells fire sparsely; the spike starts 20-30 um out along the axon (Schmidt-Hieber 2008). AA0573 sits in the lower (infrapyramidal) blade.
steps.lab: PTEN loss in granule cells makes them hypertrophic, with ectopic somata, hilar basal dendrites and mossy fibres sprouting back into the inner molecular layer, and is enough to cause epilepsy (Pun et al. 2012).

steps.title: The mossy fibre
steps.say: Through the hilus (collaterals here feed mossy cells and interneurons), then along CA3 in stratum lucidum.

velocity.source: Mossy fibre, mouse slices (Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger 2008).

steps.title: Giant bouton on a CA3 thorn
steps.say: The mossy fibre meets CA3 cell AA0307 (gap 12.6 um, closed by 12.6 um).

steps.title: Inward to the CA3 soma
steps.say: Proximal apical dendrite to the cell body.

steps.title: The CA3 cell fires
steps.say: CA3 pyramidal cells also excite each other through recurrent collaterals (the CA side loop ride follows one).

steps.title: A Schaffer collateral
steps.say: The axon arcs out of CA3 into CA1, where it runs in radiatum and oriens.

steps.title: Synapse on a CA1 dendrite
steps.say: The Schaffer collateral meets CA1 cell AA0306 in CA1SO (gap 53.4 um, closed by moving the CA1 cell 53 um: within registration error).

steps.title: Inward to the CA1 soma
steps.say: From the basal dendrite in oriens to the cell body.

steps.title: The CA1 cell fires
steps.say: CA1 is the main output of the hippocampus proper.

steps.title: Out to the subiculum
steps.say: CA1 axons run through the alveus and end in the subiculum; AA0306 puts 21 mm of axon there.

velocity.source: Pyramidal axon, assumed like CA3 (Meeks & Mennerick 2007).

steps.title: The loop closes in deep EC
steps.say: The subiculum (and CA1) project to the deep layers of the entorhinal cortex, which send the result back to the neocortex and to layers II and III.

rides.label: DS1: lateral volley
rides.blurb: Many LEC layer II cells fire together; their axons depolarize the outer third of the molecular layer: a sink there.

steps.title: LEC layer II fires together
steps.say: Two real LEC cells stand for the population (AA1047, AA1002).
steps.lab: DS1: sink in the outer molecular layer, both blades (Bragin et al. 1995).

steps.title: The volley
steps.say: Along the lateral perforant path, together.

velocity.source: Perforant path volley, rabbit in vivo (Lomo 1971).

steps.title: Sink in OML
steps.say: The outer third of the molecular layer goes negative (a current sink); the return current makes a source closer to the granule cells.
steps.lab: This is the profile your probe records across the dentate: the sink at OML, the source in MML and the granule layer.

steps.title: Hilar interneurons burst
steps.say: Dentate spikes come with bursts of hilar interneurons (Bragin 1995).

rides.label: DS2: medial volley
rides.blurb: Many MEC layer II stellate cells fire together; their axons depolarize the middle third: a sink there.

steps.title: MEC layer II stellate cells fire together
steps.say: A real stellate cell (slice tracing, Huang 2024) stands for the population. No public registered MEC layer II tracing has an axon, so the medial perforant path below is drawn along its route in the atlas (angular bundle, subiculum, fissure).
steps.lab: DS2: sink in the middle molecular layer (Bragin et al. 1995). DS2 is usually the larger dentate spike.

steps.title: The medial perforant path (drawn)
steps.say: Drawn, not traced: the cheapest route through the atlas's entorhinal deep layers, angular path, subiculum and fissure to MML.

steps.title: Sink in MML
steps.say: The middle third goes negative, flanked by sources in the outer third and the granule layer.

steps.title: Hilar interneurons burst
steps.say: Feed-forward drive reaches basket cells too: granule-cell somata are clamped a few ms later.

rides.label: Dentate local circuit
rides.blurb: Granule cell to mossy cell to granule cells far away, and the three interneurons that answer.

steps.title: The granule cell fires
steps.say: AA0573 again, in the lower blade.

steps.title: A hilar collateral
steps.say: On its way to CA3 the mossy fibre branches in the hilus.

velocity.source: Mossy fibre, mouse slices (Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger 2008).

steps.title: On a mossy cell's thorn
steps.say: The drawn mossy cell's thick proximal dendrite ends on this collateral.

steps.title: Inward to the mossy cell
steps.say: Thorny excrescences crowd the proximal dendrites.

steps.title: The mossy cell fires
steps.say: Mossy cells are far more active than granule cells (Senzai & Buzsaki 2017).
steps.lab: Mossy cells are lost or damaged in many epilepsy models; whether the survivors excite or inhibit granule cells is the "dormant basket cell" debate (Scharfman 2016).

steps.title: To another level
steps.say: The axon runs through the hilus and inner molecular layer, along the hippocampus, to granule cells at other levels (drawn route).

velocity.source: Mossy-cell axon, assumed like mossy fibres (slower in imaging: Ma et al. 2017).

steps.title: On a far granule cell
steps.say: The associational synapse: a granule cell's proximal dendrite in the inner molecular layer (MouseLight AA0869).

steps.title: Inward
steps.say: A proximal input, close to the soma.

steps.title: A granule cell elsewhere is excited
steps.say: The dentate talks along its own length through mossy cells.

steps.title: The HIPP cell answers
steps.say: Mossy-fibre collaterals also drive hilar interneurons; this SST+ HIPP cell (slice tracing, placed by its layers) fires.
steps.lab: In a Kcnt1 gain-of-function mouse, non-fast-spiking interneurons such as SST+ cells are less excitable (Shore et al. 2020).

steps.title: Out to the distal dendrites
steps.say: HIPP axons fill the outer two-thirds of the molecular layer.

steps.title: Inhibition where the perforant path lands
steps.say: On the granule cell's distal dendrite.

steps.title: The basket cell
steps.say: PV+ basket cell (slice tracing, placed by its layers).

steps.title: To the soma
steps.say: A dense basket in the granule layer.

steps.title: Perisomatic inhibition
steps.say: On the granule cell's soma.

steps.title: The chandelier cell
steps.say: Axo-axonic cell (slice tracing).

steps.title: To the axon initial segment
steps.say: Cartridges at the granule-layer / hilus border.

steps.title: The last word
steps.say: On the axon initial segment, where the granule cell's spike starts.

rides.label: CA side loops
rides.blurb: CA3 exciting CA3, entorhinal layer III straight onto CA1 tufts, and the O-LM cell that guards them.

steps.title: A CA3 cell fires
steps.say: AA0307 again.

steps.title: A recurrent collateral
steps.say: Back into CA3 radiatum and oriens.

steps.title: On another CA3 cell
steps.say: CA3 cell AA0304 (gap 4.6 um).

steps.title: The second CA3 cell fires
steps.say: Pattern completion needs just this: cells that fire together, wired together.

steps.title: EC layer III fires
steps.say: No public tracing of an EC layer III axon reaches CA1, so this path is drawn along its route in the atlas.

steps.title: The temporoammonic path (drawn)
steps.say: Through the angular bundle and subiculum to stratum lacunosum-moleculare.

steps.title: On the CA1 tuft
steps.say: Direct cortical input on the distal tuft of AA0306.

steps.title: Down the apical dendrite
steps.say: A long way in: distal tuft inputs are filtered on their way to the soma.

steps.title: A local collateral in oriens
steps.say: CA1 axons give collaterals in oriens before leaving.

velocity.source: Pyramidal axon, assumed like CA3 (Meeks & Mennerick 2007).

steps.title: Onto the O-LM cell
steps.say: The O-LM cell's horizontal dendrites in oriens (gap 11 um, shown as a short hop).

steps.title: The O-LM cell fires
steps.say: SST+ O-LM cells feed back onto the same tufts the temporoammonic path excites.
steps.lab: SST+ interneurons are among the cells a Kcnt1 gain-of-function variant makes less excitable (Shore et al. 2020; 2024).

steps.title: Up to lacunosum-moleculare
steps.say: Across the layers to slm.

steps.title: Inhibition on the tuft
steps.say: CA1 gates its own entorhinal input.

note: Cells from different mice, aligned by registration to the Allen CCF (good to about 50-100 um). A synapse here is a close approach in that shared frame; cells were moved by the gap (listed) to close it.
